questions.q: What are the two real trigger types Flow Designer offers?
options: Record trigger and Scheduled trigger
Approval trigger and Rejection trigger
Manual trigger and Automatic trigger
Script trigger and Catalog trigger
questions.explain: Flow Designer offers a Record trigger (reacting to a record change) and a Scheduled trigger (firing on a time-based schedule).

questions.q: What happens if you set a Record trigger to fire on "Created" for the Incident table with no condition set?
options: The flow never fires at all
The trigger fires on every single new Incident, regardless of priority or category
The trigger automatically waits for a manager's approval first
The trigger only fires once per day no matter how many Incidents are created
questions.explain: Without a condition narrowing it down, a Record trigger set to Created fires on every new record on that table — a condition is what narrows it to the records that should actually matter.

questions.q: How does a Record trigger's condition work, according to this lesson?
options: It uses a unique syntax found nowhere else on the platform
It uses the same condition-builder pattern already used for Business Rules and ACLs in earlier courses
It can only be configured through a custom script
It applies only to the Scheduled trigger, not the Record trigger
questions.explain: The Record trigger's condition builder is the same condition-builder pattern used for Business Rules and ACLs, just applied inside Flow Designer.

questions.q: What is the Scheduled trigger most similar to, from an earlier course in this path?
options: ACLs
Business Rules
Scheduled Jobs
Catalog Items
questions.explain: A Scheduled trigger is the same underlying idea as a Scheduled Job, just expressed natively inside Flow Designer instead of as a separate scheduled script.

questions.q: Per this lesson's decision rule, which requirement clearly calls for a Scheduled trigger rather than a Record trigger?
options: "When a Change Request gets approved, notify the implementer"
"As soon as a new Incident comes in with Priority Critical, alert the on-call team"
"Every morning at 7am, send a summary of each team's open Incidents"
"When a Catalog request is submitted, start the fulfillment process"
questions.explain: "Every morning at 7am" is time-based, not reacting to a record change — that's exactly what a Scheduled trigger is for; the other three options all react to something happening, which calls for a Record trigger.
